 Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- from the respondents, for the damage caused to the car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 of the petitioner, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 01-03-2023 at about 22:45 to 22:46 p.m., the driver of petitioner's car bearing Reg. No.KA-03-MR-8377 was driving the same by following the traffic rules and regulations.

When he reached near NICE office, at nice road towards Mysore road,
Bengaluru city, at that time suddenly the driver of lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-19-AB-2471 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the car of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner's car got fully damaged.
On account of the said damage the petitioner was unable to use the said car as usual for his daily routine work.
Further the petitioner being a power of attorney holder of the said car got repaired the same by spending amount more than Rs.5,00,000/-.
Further, the petitioner has suffered great hardship due to non-availability of said car for his day to day work.
The Kengeri Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said lorry for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, it is prayed to allow Secretary Of Sb Education Trust vs Reliance Gen Ins Co Ltd on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55112677/
2 the petition and award compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- with interest.

sentences.text: 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their respective counsel.
The respondent No.2 has filed his written statement.
In view of order dated 18-12-2025 on I.A.No.-IV, the name of respondent No.1 is deleted from the petition.
4. The respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
Further, he has contended that, there is inordinate delay in filing the present petition and as such, in view of provisions of amended Motor Vehicles Act, the petition is not maintainable.
He has admitted that, he is the owner of the lorry bearing No.KA-19-AB-2471, which is duly insured with respondent No.1 and policy was valid and in force as on the date of accident.
He has denied the occurrence of the accident.

He has contended that, at the time of alleged incident, the lorry was operated by a duly authorized driver, who had possessed a valid driving licence and was driving the said vehicle with due care, by following applicable laws and regulations.
The alleged accident is caused solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car of the petitioner and hence, no liability can be imposed on either the respondent No.1 or respondent No.2.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Further it is contended that, his lorry was insured with respondent No.1 and the policy was valid and in force and driver of his vehicle was holding valid and effective driving licence.
In the event this Court comes to conclusion that, the petitioner is entitled to any compensation, the same is to be borne solely by respondent No.1.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed for dismissal of the petition.

Whether the petitioner proves that, his car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 was damaged in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 01-03-2023 at about 10.45 to 10.46 p.m., due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.KA- 19-AB-2471 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or award ?

it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.KA-19-AB-2471 and dashing the same to ongoing car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 of the petitioner.

But, the respondent No.2 has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and he has taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 and there was no fault on the part of the driver of lorry bearing Reg.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that,
the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AB- 2471 and dashing the same to ongoing car bearing No.KA- 03-MR-8377 of the petitioner and due to said impact the front right side wheel tyre and wheel disc, front right side rear view mirror, right side both front door and rear door and front right side wheel fender of the said car are damaged.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

13. Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazer and Ex.P.4 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 40 feet wide NICE road, which leads towards Mysore, near NICE Office, Bengaluru City, in between offending lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AB-2471 and ongoing car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377.

As per the Motor Vehicles Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.8,
the accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing No.KA- 03-MR-8377,
then in the given facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-19-AB-2471.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the alleged accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-19-AB-2471 and dashing the same to the car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the owner or the driver of said vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry and damages caused to the car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 in the said accident.
14. The Ex.P.8 Motor Vehicle Accident Report clearly speaks that, the car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 is extensively damaged in the accident in question.

As per the said report, the front right side wheel tyre and wheel disc, front right side rear view mirror, right side both front door and rear doors and front right side wheel fender of the said car are damaged.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the said report.
There is nothing on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner, with respect to cause of accident and damage caused to the car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377.

No.KA-19-AB- 2471.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, lorry bearing No.KA-19-AB-2471 was damaged in the road traffic accident, occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing No.KA-19-AB-2471.

Further, the Ex.P.8 Motor Vehicle Accident Report is clear evident that, the front right side wheel tyre and wheel disc, front right side rear view mirror, right side both front door and rear doors and front right side wheel fender of the said car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377 are damaged in the said accident.
The Ex.P.12 tax invoice are also clear evident of above stated damage to the car bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377.
The oral evidence of P.W.1 is fully corroborated by the documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner.
19. As per Ex.P.12 tax invoice, the total expenses incurred for repair of damage caused to the car bearing No. No.KA- 03-MR-8377 is Rs.3,43,840/-.
No doubt, the petitioner has not examined the author of said document to prove the contents of said documents.
But, as there is no contrary evidence on record there is absolutely no reason to disbelieve the said document.
Further, there is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no impediment to hold that, the petitioner has spent Rs.3,43,840/- towards the repair of damages' caused to its car bearing No.
No.KA-03- MR-8377 in the accident in question.
Accordingly, it is held that, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.3,43,840/- for the damage caused to its car.
20. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending lorry bearing No.KA-03-MR-8377.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-19-AB-2471 the accident has occurred and the car bearing No. KA-03-MR-8377 belonging to the petitioner was damaged in the said accident.

The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,43,840/- (Rupees three lakh forty three thousand eight hundred and forty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
